reader.requirement: At 1985 the temporary is then combined with or transferred to each resultant in the left-to-right order written, each resultant identified (subscripts evaluated) when it is reached, so ADD a, b, c TO c, d (c), e uses the updated c to subscript d and MULTIPLY a (i) BY i, a (i) uses the updated i; the witnesses cover ADD TO, COMPUTE and DIVIDE REMAINDER with a subscript changed by an earlier receiver but not the clause's own MULTIPLY a (i) BY i, a (i) example or an ODO object as an earlier receiver.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal: at 1985 a receiver whose store fails without a phrase keeps its content and the next receiver is still stored (GuardedStore per receiver in either arm)

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|DialectBehaviors|EditionContext|CobolVersion over ArithmeticEmitter.cs, ReceiverBracketEmitter.cs, ExpressionBinder.cs, PlaceIdentification.cs: the receiver loop order and the identified-at-store resolution consult no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: identical output at --std 85 and --std 2023 for the clause's two examples
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the clause's MULTIPLY a (i) BY i, a (i) example and an ODO object updated by an earlier receiver are not in the witnesses

probes.expected: the clause's examples: a=b=c=1 -> temp 3, c=4, d(4)=13, e=23; a=(2,3,4), i=1 -> temp 2, i=2, a(2)=6
OE (N) identified after N is stored: OE(3) = 1 + 1
the receivers to the right of an overflowing one are still stored in order

reader.notes: The receiver loop stores left to right and each receiver's Place is identified at store (ResolveReceivingAtStore / debug.IdentifiedAtStore), so a subscript or ODO object changed by an earlier resultant selects the element the clause's equivalent sequence selects. Both examples printed in the clause give the equivalent-sequence result at --std 85.
